topStories.headline: Muni's Survival on the November Ballot: What Prop H Means for West Portal and Stonestown Riders
topStories.dek: A parcel-tax measure on the November 3 ballot would fill roughly half of Muni's $307 million annual deficit — or riders on the K, M, and local bus lines could face steep cuts.
topStories.body:
Voters across San Francisco will decide Proposition H on November 3, a measure that would impose a 15-year annual parcel tax on most properties in the city to fund Muni operations. The Golden Gate Xpress reported on October 28 that without the revenue, the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency faces a budget hole of more than $300 million a year once pandemic-era relief funding is exhausted.

For neighborhoods served by the K Ingleside and M Ocean View lines — which pass through West Portal station and stop at Stonestown Galleria — the stakes are concrete. The SFMTA has warned that a funding failure could force it to eliminate as many as 19 to 20 bus routes and a streetcar line while cutting frequency across the network. The K and M together carry tens of thousands of riders daily through these neighborhoods.

Prop H is designed to work alongside a separate regional measure, the Connect Bay Area Act (RTM), also on the November 3 ballot. Together the two measures are projected to close Muni's full operating gap. Prop H alone is estimated to generate between $177 million and $184 million annually, covering roughly half the deficit, according to the SF Public Press.

District 7 Supervisor Myrna Melgar, whose district includes West Portal, Forest Hill, and St. Francis Wood, publicly supports both measures. A report from the San Francisco Controller's Office found that if Prop H passes, it could support nearly 1,500 jobs over 15 years and generate around $400 million in broader economic activity. Opponents have raised concerns about passing new tax burdens onto renters through landlord pass-throughs.

topStories.headline: SFSU Launches Campus-Wide Career Initiative as Enrollment Rises for First Time in Over a Decade
topStories.dek: University President Lynn Mahoney announced the Future-Ready Workforce Initiative in mid-October, pairing a new senior hire focused on employer partnerships with SFSU's strongest incoming class in years.
topStories.body:
San Francisco State University marked two milestones in October: its first year-over-year enrollment increase in more than ten years, and the launch of a new campus-wide effort to connect graduates with careers. President Lynn Mahoney announced the Future-Ready Workforce Initiative on October 15 at the university's annual Fall Career and Internship Fair.

SFSU enrolled 20,824 students for fall 2026, including a 20 percent lift in new incoming undergraduate enrollment compared to the previous year and an 18 percent increase in total new incoming students across undergraduate and graduate programs. University officials called it a significant turnaround after years of demographic headwinds and declining enrollment.

The new initiative brings together faculty, students, alumni, administration, and a newly created senior leadership role: Inés C. Barbosa joined SFSU this fall as its first assistant vice president for workforce partnerships, tasked with expanding employer relationships and internship pipelines. The program also draws on SFSU's network of more than 300,000 alumni to provide mentorships aligned with students' fields of study.

Mayor Daniel Lurie praised the effort at the fair, saying the city wants SFSU graduates to build their futures in San Francisco. The enrollment rebound is particularly significant for the Lakeshore and Parkmerced neighborhoods, which have long relied on the university's student population as an economic anchor.

topStories.headline: Parkmerced's Development Land Sold to New York Investor as Complex Emerges From Financial Turmoil
topStories.dek: Yellowstone Real Estate Investments acquired four parcels approved for nearly 1,700 new apartments in July, but whether construction will actually begin remains an open question.
topStories.body:
The long-troubled Parkmerced complex took another turn in its ownership saga this summer when Yellowstone Real Estate Investments, a New York-based firm, purchased four land parcels within the 152-acre property. The SF Chronicle reported the deal in late July, noting that the parcels carry approvals for close to 1,700 new apartments alongside 52 existing units. The sale came after Maximus Real Estate Partners defaulted on Parkmerced's $1.8 billion loan, sending the complex into foreclosure.

Yellowstone's chief executive Isaac Hera announced the acquisition on LinkedIn, describing it as a completion of the takeover of Parkmerced's development land and expressing enthusiasm for the site's long-term potential. The firm had previously provided a $101 million construction loan to the project, which gave it a path to the acquisition bid.

Whether the new owner will break ground on additional housing is not yet clear. The Chronicle noted that the company had not announced any construction timeline. The existing occupied portions of Parkmerced — more than 3,200 units housing roughly 9,000 residents — remain under separate management by Ballast's property management company, Brick + Timber, following court-supervised intervention by special servicer Douglas Wilson Companies.

For neighbors and SFSU students who depend on Parkmerced's affordability and proximity to campus, the transition represents both a potential source of new housing and continued uncertainty about conditions at the complex, which residents have previously described as plagued by maintenance backlogs and security concerns.

events.location: Your assigned polling place, San Francisco

moreNews.headline: Raising Cane's Draws 200-Person Opening Day Crowd at Stonestown Galleria
moreNews.body: The chicken-finger chain opened its second San Francisco location at Stonestown Galleria on Monday, October 13, drawing more than 200 customers, including some who camped overnight to be first in line. The grand opening included giveaways and a donation to the nonprofit Children's Book Project, which distributes books to underserved children. Stonestown, which added extended Friday and Saturday hours in August after reaching near-zero vacancy rates, continues to attract new tenants while downtown San Francisco Centre sits empty.

moreNews.headline: SFSU's 2027 Commencement Set for Oracle Park on May 21
moreNews.body: San Francisco State University announced in its October 12 campus memo that the Class of 2027 commencement ceremony will be held on Friday, May 21, 2027, at Oracle Park, home of the San Francisco Giants. The venue choice follows the university's enrollment rebound, which brought total fall 2026 enrollment to 20,824 students.
